rules.label: Authority Leakage
rules.typical_structure:
This pattern commonly appears when material:

- Uses confident tone without mandate
- Is reused in contexts with higher stakes
- Lacks clear audience or decision boundary
- Migrates from internal to external use

---

rules.label: Constraint Inversion
rules.typical_structure:
This pattern commonly appears when material:

- Treats safety, compliance, or metrics as success criteria
- Optimizes proxies while losing the underlying objective
- Reframes limitations as defining features
- Preserves form while hollowing out function
- Enforces rules that undermine their original intent

The inversion is often gradual and implicit.

---

rules.label: Population-Level Evidence vs Individual-Level Recommendation
rules.description: This contradiction arises in medical guideline reasoning and preventive health recommendations.
rules.stop_condition:
This contradiction triggers STOP due to illegitimate level transfer
(population → individual without admissible bridging conditions).

rules.label: Descriptive Statement Used as Normative Authorization
rules.description: Common in ethics-adjacent policy arguments and expert recommendations.

rules.label: Implicit Assumption Conflict
rules.typical_structure:
This pattern commonly appears when material:

- Mixes incompatible world models without acknowledgment
- Assumes different default states in different sections
- Relies on background conditions that cannot coexist
- Shifts foundational premises without signaling a transition
- Treats contextual assumptions as universal

Because the assumptions are implicit,
the contradiction often goes unnoticed until stress is applied.

rules.label: Population-Level Evidence vs Individual-Level Recommendation
rules.description: Common in medicine, public health, and policy guidelines.
rules.stop_condition: Illegitimate level transfer (population → individual without admissible bridging conditions)

rules.label: Proxy Measure Treated as the Target Outcome
rules.description: Common in medicine, economics, and management metrics.

rules.label: Role Confusion
rules.typical_structure:
This pattern commonly appears when material:

- Alternates between descriptive and prescriptive voice
- Mixes observer, participant, and authority perspectives
- Treats analysis as decision, or decision as analysis
- Assumes responsibility without mandate
- Uses “we”, “one”, or “the system” ambiguously

Because role shifts are implicit,
the resulting contradictions are often subtle.

---

rules.label: Scope Collapse
rules.typical_structure:
This pattern commonly appears when material:

- Moves from local to global claims without justification
- Treats examples as general rules
- Applies exploratory results as operational guidance
- Extends conclusions across domains, scales, or contexts
- Collapses distinctions between “in this case” and “in general”

The transition is usually implicit,
making the scope shift difficult to detect.

---

rules.label: Temporal Misalignment
rules.typical_structure:
This pattern commonly appears when material:

- Treats snapshots as stable states
- Applies historical assumptions to current conditions
- Mixes real-time and delayed feedback loops
- Assumes permanence where decay or drift exists
- Ignores versioning or lifecycle boundaries

---

rules.label: Uncertainty Acknowledged, Action Presented as Settled
rules.description: Common in risk communication and crisis narratives.
rules.stop_condition: Uncertainty collapse / implicit decision rule injection
